```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "A names a specific customer: a Wisconsin public adjuster plus an affiliated roofing contractor, with a documented intake pain. For a 90-day paying-customer goal, a reachable named buyer counts for more than market size. B names no customer at all.",
    "A's willingness-to-pay is directly sourced. At least four direct competitors (ClaimWizard, Claim Titan, claimOS, AdjustCRM) publish $49–$250/mo pricing to the same buyer type. That shows this buyer already pays for software in this category.",
    "A's demand evidence comes from the payer segment itself: a PA firm's ops director and a small PA on r/CRM. B's demand quotes come from family members helping elderly parents, who are not the stated B2B payer.",
    "B faces a zero price floor. Microsoft Quick Assist ships free on Windows and JoinByKey is free and markets no-download support. Paid incumbents already target the 'any technical ability' customer, so a new entrant has no clear wedge.",
    "B's likely paying buyers in healthcare, financial and other regulated verticals bring SOC 2, HIPAA/BAA and SSO expectations that cannot credibly be met in six weeks. A's compliance burden (WI Insurance Data Security Law, breach notice) is real but narrower and tied to a single buyer.",
    "A's main drawbacks are a small market (188 WI PAs) and scope creep toward full claim-lifecycle features. These limit the long-term ceiling more than they block a first paying customer within 90 days."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence does not match its payer. All three quotes (two from an Apple Support Community thread, one from r/it) come from individuals trying to help their own elderly parents, not from support-team managers or CX leads, who are the hypothesized payer. B's own case-against admits this segment defaults to free tools. The cited vendor-marketing gains (41% faster resolution, 47% higher first-contact resolution) carry no source in the brief and so count as missing.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. A's edge rests heavily on the affiliated customer pair, and the brief flags that this commitment's reality and recurrence are unverified. AdjustEdge's pricing was also not confirmed on re-check. If the customer relationship is informal, A's advantage narrows considerably, though B would still lack any identified paying buyer."
}
```
